newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers still slipping.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers still slipping.

text.p: Some rail and truck offers in U.S. soymeal cash markets were lower Wednesday in response to weak demand from end-users, dealers said.
"The market isn't doing much today (Wednesday), but it is still high enough to kill any business," said one dealer in the Southeast.
Recent 8-1/2 year highs in CBOT soymeal prices have shut-off forward demand from domestic users, and some report a softening in export demand for U.S. soymeal.
In response, many soybean processors are said to be cutting back on soymeal and soyoil production this week, dealers said.
Most expect the pace of this week's crush to come off the recent historically-high 30 million bushel level.
Flood waters in the Ohio River Valley have receded in a number of areas, and dealers report some barge traffic moving.
"The water's coming down," said one Kentucky broker on the Ohio River. "We've dropped a couple of feet in the last 24 hours.
